components.note: 立 depicts a person standing with arms and legs spread, on a horizontal line representing the ground — a simple picture of standing upright.
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 谈判双方在这个问题上的立场完全不同。
example.pinyin: tánpàn shuāngfāng zài zhège wèntí shàng de lìchǎng wánquán bùtóng.
example.english: The two sides in the negotiation have completely different positions on this issue.
example.fact: The 1978 Camp David Accords succeeded partly because U.S. mediators kept Egypt and Israel's negotiating teams in separate cabins for much of the thirteen days, preventing face-to-face clashes over entrenched positions and letting written proposals shuttle back and forth instead. The technique, sometimes called "single-text negotiation," is still taught in diplomatic training today.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.
士 (a scholar/gentleman) — represents a person of learning and ambition.
心 (heart/mind) — the mind and aspirations of a scholar gave 志 its meaning 'purpose, will, ambition.'

example.hanzi: 她凭着坚强的意志完成了马拉松比赛。
example.pinyin: tā píngzhe jiānqiáng de yìzhì wánchéngle mǎlāsōng bǐsài.
example.english: She finished the marathon through sheer willpower.
example.fact: The Comrades Marathon in South Africa, first run in 1921, covers roughly 90 kilometers between Durban and Pietermaritzburg and has a strict twelve-hour cutoff enforced by officials who physically pull exhausted runners off the course the instant the finish-line gun fires. Finishers within the cutoff earn a bronze, silver, or gold medal depending on their time, but anyone even a second late receives nothing.

components.note: 亻 (person) — one person.
二 (two) — a second person, together showing a caring relationship between two people, giving 仁 its meaning 'humaneness, benevolence.'
心 (heart) — 慈 describes a warm, kind-hearted feeling toward others.
兹 (zī) shares the rhyme -i with cí, and both use dental sibilant initials (c/z) — only the aspiration and tone differ.

example.hanzi: 国王以仁慈著称,从不轻易处死囚犯。
example.pinyin: guówáng yǐ réncí zhùchēng, cóng bù qīngyì chǔsǐ qiúfàn.
example.english: The king was known for his benevolence and rarely executed prisoners.
example.fact: Emperor Ashoka of ancient India, after a brutal conquest of Kalinga around 261 BC, reportedly renounced further warfare and had edicts carved on pillars across his empire promoting nonviolence, animal welfare, and care for the sick. Several of these Ashokan pillars, including the one at Sarnath topped by four lions, still stand today, and the lion capital was later adopted as modern India's national emblem.

components.note: 手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.
毛 (fur, hair) — 表 originally pictured a fur garment worn on the outside.
衣 (clothing) — an outer fur wrap gave 表 its meaning of 'outer' or 'surface,' and later, 'to express' (showing something on the surface).

example.hanzi: 他的手表是爷爷留给他的传家宝。
example.pinyin: tā de shǒubiǎo shì yéye liú gěi tā de chuánjiābǎo.
example.english: His wristwatch is a family heirloom left to him by his grandfather.
example.fact: Wristwatches only became standard for men after World War I; before that they were considered mainly a woman's accessory, while men carried pocket watches. Soldiers in the trenches found pocket watches impractical to check under fire, so many strapped them to their wrists with leather cuffs, a battlefield workaround that permanently shifted men's fashion once the soldiers came home.

components.note: 阝 (mound/place) — on the left side, a form of 阜 (mound, earthworks), often relating to terrain, elevation, or place.
遂 (suí, also suì) gives the sound — an exact match with 隧's reading.
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.

example.hanzi: 这条隧道穿过阿尔卑斯山,连接了两个国家。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo suìdào chuānguò ā'ěrbēisī shān, liánjiēle liǎng gè guójiā.
example.english: This tunnel passes through the Alps, connecting two countries.
example.fact: The Gotthard Base Tunnel in Switzerland, opened in 2016, runs 57 kilometers through the Alps and is the world's longest railway tunnel — engineers had to bore through rock reaching 45°C and account for the mountain settling by several centimeters as material was removed. It cut the Zurich-to-Milan rail journey by roughly an hour.

components.note: 王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — a valuable object one might glimpse or notice.
见 (to see) — catching sight of something links to the meanings 'to appear, present, now.'
亻 (person) — 代 relates to a person's place in time.
弋 (a stake used to mark or catch something) — combined with 亻 (person), 代 came to mean a 'generation' or 'era,' and 'to take the place of' someone.

example.hanzi: 这座博物馆展示了从古代到现代的艺术发展。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò bówùguǎn zhǎnshìle cóng gǔdài dào xiàndài de yìshù fāzhǎn.
example.english: This museum shows the development of art from ancient times to the modern era.
example.fact: The Bauhaus school, founded in Weimar, Germany in 1919, fused fine art with industrial craft and pioneered much of what is now called modern design — clean geometric forms, exposed materials, and furniture meant for mass production rather than individual commission. The Nazi government forced it to close in 1933, but its exiled teachers, including Walter Gropius and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, carried its ideas into American architecture schools.

components.note: 寸 (a hand) — guiding the way.
巳 (a place) — the destination being pointed toward, giving 导 its meaning 'to lead, guide, direct.'
弓 (bow) — 弹 relates to a projectile shot from a bow, like a pellet
单 (dān) gives a loose sound connection to 弹's reading dàn

example.hanzi: 这个国家最近测试了一种新型导弹。
example.pinyin: zhège guójiā zuìjìn cèshìle yī zhǒng xīnxíng dǎodàn.
example.english: This country recently tested a new type of guided missile.
example.fact: The German V-2, first launched operationally in 1944, was the world's first long-range guided ballistic missile, reaching an altitude of about 80 kilometers — effectively becoming the first man-made object to cross into space. Its lead engineer, Wernher von Braun, later became a key figure in the American Apollo program that put astronauts on the Moon.

components.note: The traditional form 無 originally pictured a person dancing while holding decorated sleeves or feathers, likely part of a shamanic ritual dance. That picture was borrowed early on for the unrelated grammatical meaning 'not, without,' and the simplified 无 keeps only a trace of the original image.
比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'

example.hanzi: 站在山顶俯瞰云海,那种壮观景象无比震撼。
example.pinyin: zhàn zài shāndǐng fǔkàn yúnhǎi, nà zhǒng zhuàngguān jǐngxiàng wúbǐ zhènhàn.
example.english: Standing on the mountaintop looking down at the sea of clouds, the spectacular view was incomparably stunning.
example.fact: The "sea of clouds" seen from mountain peaks like Mount Emei in China forms when moist air is trapped below a temperature inversion layer, condensing into a flat cloud deck that fills the valleys while the peaks stay clear above it. Meteorologists call this a subsidence inversion, and it is most common during calm, high-pressure weather.

meanings: a period of time in the recent past
(indicating a period of time up to the present) all along

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.

向 pictures a simple hut with an opening below a roof, representing the direction one faces when looking out through a doorway or window. That image of facing outward toward something gave the character its meaning 'toward, direction.'

example.hanzi: 他一向对朋友很讲信用。
example.pinyin: tā yīxiàng duì péngyou hěn jiǎng xìnyòng.
example.english: He has always been trustworthy with his friends.
example.fact: Trust between strangers underpins the entire diamond trade in cities like Antwerp, where deals worth millions of dollars are still sealed with a handshake and the Yiddish phrase "mazal und broche" (luck and blessing) rather than a written contract. The system relies on tight-knit merchant networks where a single broken promise can permanently blacklist a trader from the community.

components.note: 成 traces back to an oracle-bone picture of a halberd-like weapon with an added stroke, likely marking the finishing blow that ended a battle or campaign. That sense of a task being brought to a close gave 成 its meaning 'to complete, to succeed.'
立 depicts a person standing with arms and legs spread, on a horizontal line representing the ground — a simple picture of standing upright.

example.hanzi: 这家公司于1998年正式成立。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī yú yījiǔjiǔbā nián zhèngshì chénglì.
example.english: This company was officially established in 1998.
example.fact: Google was legally established as a company on September 4, 1998, in a garage in Menlo Park, California, rented from Susan Wojcicki, who later became CEO of YouTube. The garage was preserved and is now marked with a small plaque commemorating it as the search engine's first office.

components.note: 舌 (tongue) — taste is sensed on the tongue.
甘 (sweet, tasty) contributes to the character's form, naming the flavor itself.
虫 (insect) — honey is made by bees, which are insects.
宓 (mì) gives the sound — an exact match for 蜜.

example.hanzi: 他们度过了一段甜蜜的蜜月旅行。
example.pinyin: tāmen dùguòle yī duàn tiánmì de mìyuè lǚxíng.
example.english: They spent a sweet honeymoon trip together.
example.fact: Bees keep their hive within about one degree of 35°C year-round by clustering and vibrating their wing muscles in winter or fanning and spreading water droplets in summer, a feat of collective thermoregulation that helps honey — which never spoils under proper storage — stay edible even centuries later, as shown by jars found in ancient Egyptian tombs.

components.note: 里 (village, a unit of land) — 野 describes open country beyond the village.
予 (yǔ) reflects an older phonetic link, though the modern readings yě and yǔ have since diverged.
丷 (horns) at the top shows the animal's horns.
田 (here shaped like a head with eyes) in the middle represents the animal's face.
口 (mouth) at the bottom completes the creature's face, giving 兽 its meaning 'beast, animal.'

example.hanzi: 森林深处传来野兽的吼叫声。
example.pinyin: sēnlín shēnchù chuánlái yěshòu de hǒujiào shēng.
example.english: The roar of a wild beast came from deep in the forest.
example.fact: The Siberian tiger, the largest wild cat species alive, can weigh over 300 kilograms and once ranged across a vast swath of the Russian Far East, Korea, and northeast China. Intensive conservation since the 1940s, when fewer than 40 remained, has brought the wild population back to several hundred individuals today.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 移 originally described transplanting rice seedlings from a nursery bed to a paddy, an early agricultural act of 'moving' something to a new place.
多 (duō) carries a sound distantly related to yí; the two readings share little today after centuries of pronunciation drift.
木 (tree) — 植 relates to planting trees and other plants.
直 (zhí) gives the sound — an exact match with 植's reading zhí.

example.hanzi: 医生成功完成了这次心脏移植手术。
example.pinyin: yīshēng chénggōng wánchéngle zhè cì xīnzàng yízhí shǒushù.
example.english: The doctors successfully completed this heart transplant surgery.
example.fact: The first successful human heart transplant was performed in 1967 by South African surgeon Christiaan Barnard, whose patient, Louis Washkansky, survived eighteen days before dying of pneumonia caused by the immunosuppressive drugs. Modern heart transplant recipients now often live well over a decade thanks to better anti-rejection medications developed in the 1980s.

components.note: 木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'

The oracle-bone form of 事 pictured a hand gripping a forked staff or ritual banner, an image tied to an official recording or managing business. That sense of handling official matters gave 事 its meaning 'affair, matter; to serve.'

example.hanzi: 这部电影的本事取材于一段真实的历史事件。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng de běnshì qǔcái yú yī duàn zhēnshí de lìshǐ shìjiàn.
example.english: This film's source material is drawn from a real historical event.
example.fact: The 1975 film Jaws was based on Peter Benchley's novel of the same name, which itself was partly inspired by a series of real shark attacks along the New Jersey shore in 1916 that killed four people in twelve days. Benchley later expressed regret over the film's role in fueling shark hysteria and spent much of his later life advocating for shark conservation.

meanings: (sports) to break through the opponent's defense

components.note: 穴 (a cave/hole) — the den the dog bursts from.
犬 (dog) — a dog suddenly darting out of its den gave 突 its meaning 'sudden, abrupt.'
石 (rock/stone) — 破 relates to breaking, as a rock can be broken
皮 (pí) gives a loose sound connection to 破's reading pò

example.hanzi: 科学家在癌症治疗方面取得了重大突破。
example.pinyin: kēxuéjiā zài áizhèng zhìliáo fāngmiàn qǔdéle zhòngdà tūpò.
example.english: Scientists have made a major breakthrough in cancer treatment.
example.fact: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, adapted from a bacterial immune defense mechanism first noticed in yogurt cultures, lets scientists cut and edit DNA at precise locations far more cheaply and quickly than older methods. Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing the technique, only eight years after their key paper was published.

meanings: Manhattan borough of New York City

components.note: 罒 (an eye) — held open.
又 (a hand) — pulling the eye open wide, together giving 曼 its meaning 'long, extended, graceful.'
口 (mouth) — 哈 is the sound made by the mouth while laughing
合 (hé) gives a sound related to 哈's reading hā, from an older, closer pronunciation link
页 (head) — 顿 originally related to bowing the head, i.e. a pause or stop
屯 (tún) gives a sound distantly related to 顿's reading dùn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 自由女神像就在曼哈顿附近的一个小岛上。
example.pinyin: zìyóu nǚshén xiàng jiù zài Mànhādùn fùjìn de yī gè xiǎo dǎo shàng.
example.english: The Statue of Liberty stands on a small island near Manhattan.
example.fact: Manhattan was purchased by the Dutch West India Company from the local Lenape people in 1626, according to a letter describing the deal as worth 60 guilders — a figure later popularized as "$24," though the actual value and fairness of the exchange are disputed, since the Lenape likely understood it as a temporary land-use agreement rather than an outright sale.

components.note: Woman — an old semantic root, not directly related to the modern meaning.
Gives the sound fāng, related to fáng but drifted apart over time.
石 (stone) — 碍 describes something solid, like a stone, blocking one's path.
㝵 gives a sound closely related to ài, though pronunciation has drifted somewhat over time.

example.hanzi: 噪音妨碍了他们正常的睡眠。
example.pinyin: zàoyīn fáng'àile tāmen zhèngcháng de shuìmián.
example.english: The noise interfered with their normal sleep.
example.fact: Chronic exposure to nighttime noise above about 40 decibels — roughly the level of a quiet refrigerator hum — has been linked by the World Health Organization to measurable increases in cardiovascular disease risk, because the body's stress hormone levels can rise even during sleep stages when a person never consciously wakes up.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 评 relates to speaking judgments or opinions about something
平 (píng) gives the sound — an exact match with 评's reading píng
宀 (roof) — 审 relates to a formal setting, like a courtroom, where matters are examined
申 (shēn) gives a sound close to 审's reading shěn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 评审委员会将从三十份作品中选出获奖者。
example.pinyin: píngshěn wěiyuánhuì jiāng cóng sānshí fèn zuòpǐn zhōng xuǎnchū huòjiǎngzhě.
example.english: The judging panel will select the winner from thirty entries.
example.fact: The Nobel Prize committees keep their nomination records sealed for fifty years, so historians only learned in the 2010s that Mahatma Gandhi had been nominated for the Peace Prize five times between 1937 and 1948 but never won — a gap the Nobel Foundation has publicly called one of its most significant omissions.

components.note: 冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 他向自己的爱人许下了永远的承诺。
example.pinyin: tā xiàng zìjǐ de àiren xǔxiàle yǒngyuǎn de chéngnuò.
example.english: He made an eternal promise to his beloved.
example.fact: The Taj Mahal in Agra, India, was commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in 1632 as a mausoleum for his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal, who died giving birth to their fourteenth child. It took roughly 20,000 workers and over a decade to complete, and its white marble is said to shift color from pink at dawn to golden under moonlight.

components.note: Depicts a young wheat or tree branch that has not yet borne fruit — the image of something still incomplete, the source of 未's meaning 'not yet.'
女 (woman) — 婚 relates to marriage, historically centered on the wife.
昏 (hūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 婚.
女 (woman) sits at the base of the character.
彐-shaped strokes above picture a hand holding a broom, an old image of a wife managing the household.

example.hanzi: 他终于向未婚妻求婚,并订下了婚期。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú xiàng wèihūnqī qiúhūn, bìng dìngxiàle hūnqī.
example.english: He finally proposed to his fiancée and set a wedding date.
example.fact: The diamond engagement ring tradition traces largely to a 1938 De Beers advertising campaign built around the slogan "A Diamond Is Forever," which successfully reframed a once-optional gift into a near-universal social expectation across much of the English-speaking world within about two decades.

components.note: 又 (hand), doubled — two hands side by side depict a pair, giving 双 its meaning 'pair, both, two.'
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 她双手捧着那本珍贵的古书。
example.pinyin: tā shuāngshǒu pěngzhe nà běn zhēnguì de gǔshū.
example.english: She held the precious old book with both hands.
example.fact: The human hand contains 27 bones — 8 in the wrist, 5 in the palm, and 14 in the fingers — making up roughly a quarter of all the bones in the entire body, which is part of why hand surgery is considered one of the most technically demanding specialties in orthopedics.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
八 (a hand shape) — one of two hands shown reaching toward the same object.
廾 (two hands together) — jointly holding up one object, giving 共 its meaning 'together, joint, common.'

example.hanzi: 这次旅行一共花了我们五千块钱。
example.pinyin: zhè cì lǚxíng yīgòng huāle wǒmen wǔqiān kuài qián.
example.english: This trip cost us five thousand yuan in total.
example.fact: The Grand Tour, a rite of passage for wealthy young Europeans from roughly the 1660s to the 1840s, could take a traveler through Italy, France, and Switzerland for a year or more and cost a small fortune in total — the eighteenth-century equivalent of hundreds of thousands of dollars once servants, carriages, and souvenirs were counted.

components.note: 巫 is traditionally read as a picture of a cross-shaped divining tool used by shamans in ritual — an image tied to its meaning 'wizard, shaman.'
帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'

example.hanzi: 传说中的巫师能用咒语召唤风雨。
example.pinyin: chuánshuō zhōng de wūshī néng yòng zhòuyǔ zhàohuàn fēngyǔ.
example.english: The legendary wizard could summon wind and rain with incantations.
example.fact: Archaeological evidence for shaman-like ritual specialists goes back at least 12,000 years — a grave in northern Israel known as the "Shaman of Hilazon Tachtit" held the remains of an elderly woman buried with tortoise shells, a human foot, and eagle wing bones, interpreted by archaeologists as a shamanic burial.

components.note: 石 (rock) — 碰 originally described one hard object, like a stone, striking another, giving 'to bump, to collide.'
並 (bìng) is only distantly related in sound to pèng — both use a bilabial initial (b/p), but the rhyme and tone have drifted apart.
工 (work, tool) — 巧 relates to skill in craft or work.
丂 (kǎo) gives a sound close to qiǎo.

example.hanzi: 我碰巧在机场遇到了多年不见的老同学。
example.pinyin: wǒ pèngqiǎo zài jīchǎng yù dàole duōnián bùjiàn de lǎo tóngxué.
example.english: I happened to run into an old classmate I hadn't seen in years at the airport.
example.fact: Penicillin was discovered by chance in 1928 when Alexander Fleming returned from vacation to find that mold had contaminated a petri dish of bacteria he had left out, and noticed the bacteria near the mold had died. That accidental observation eventually led to the first mass-produced antibiotic, saving an estimated hundreds of millions of lives since.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
人 (a person) — kneeling before a figure of authority, the image of receiving an order that gave 令 its meaning 'command, order; to cause.'

example.hanzi: 计算机严格按照程序员给出的指令执行任务。
example.pinyin: jìsuànjī yángé ànzhào chéngxùyuán gěichū de zhǐlìng zhíxíng rènwù.
example.english: The computer strictly executes tasks according to the instructions given by the programmer.
example.fact: The Apollo Guidance Computer that navigated astronauts to the Moon in 1969 had roughly 4 kilobytes of RAM and ran at just over 1 megahertz, millions of times slower than a modern smartphone — yet its carefully written assembly-language instruction sets were robust enough to recover from a nearly catastrophic 1202 alarm during the Apollo 11 landing itself.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match
巾 (cloth) reflects 饰's original connection to adornment made of cloth or fabric.
饣 (a form of 食, shí) gives a sound close to shì, sharing the initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 圣诞树上挂满了五颜六色的装饰品。
example.pinyin: shèngdàn shù shàng guàmǎnle wǔyánliùsè de zhuāngshì pǐn.
example.english: The Christmas tree was covered in colorful decorations.
example.fact: The tradition of decorating evergreen trees indoors is often traced to 16th-century Germany, where guild records from Freiburg describe a decorated tree as early as 1419, adorned with apples, nuts, and paper flowers long before electric lights existed — those came only after Edward Johnson, a colleague of Thomas Edison, strung the first electrically lit Christmas tree in New York in 1882.

components.note: 口 (a rock) — the boulder itself.
厂 (a cliff) — the rock lying at the base of a cliff, the source of 石's meaning 'stone, rock.'
氵 (water) — 油 names an oily liquid.
由 (yóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 油.

example.hanzi: 中东地区拥有全球最丰富的石油储量。
example.pinyin: zhōngdōng dìqū yōngyǒu quánqiú zuì fēngfù de shíyóu chǔliàng.
example.english: The Middle East holds the world's richest petroleum reserves.
example.fact: The 1859 Drake Well in Titusville, Pennsylvania, drilled to just 21 meters deep, is widely credited as the first commercial oil well in the United States, kicking off an oil boom that within a decade turned a small farming town into a hub of speculation, refineries, and, eventually, John D. Rockefeller's Standard Oil empire.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
釆 (to distinguish/sort) — 释 relates to sorting out and clarifying, i.e. 'to explain'
睪 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to 释's reading shì, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 被告缴纳了十万元保释金后获释。
example.pinyin: bèigào jiǎonàle shíwàn yuán bǎoshì jīn hòu huòshì.
example.english: The defendant was released after paying a bail of one hundred thousand yuan.
example.fact: The concept of bail dates back at least to the Statute of Westminster in 1275 in England, which formally distinguished which offenses were bailable and which were not, aiming to prevent sheriffs from arbitrarily jailing suspects indefinitely — a principle that later shaped the Eighth Amendment's protection against excessive bail in the U.S. Constitution.

components.note: The simplified 写 descends from the traditional 寫, which combined 宀 (roof) with 舄 (a magpie, used only for its sound) to describe placing or arranging something under a roof. That sense later narrowed to 'to copy down, to write.'
亻 (person) — the human party whose word is at stake.

言 (speech) — combined with 亻 (person), the image of a person standing behind their own words gave 信 its meanings 'to trust, to believe' and, by extension, 'a letter' — a trusted message carried between people.

example.hanzi: 奶奶还是喜欢用手写信给远方的亲人。
example.pinyin: nǎinai háishi xǐhuan yòng shǒu xiěxìn gěi yuǎnfāng de qīnrén.
example.english: Grandma still likes to write letters by hand to family far away.
example.fact: During World War II, British and American postal services used a technique called V-mail (Victory Mail), photographically reducing handwritten letters onto microfilm to save enormous cargo space on military transport — a single reel of film could carry the equivalent of over 1,500 kilograms of paper letters.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诊 describes a doctor asking questions and speaking with a patient to diagnose an illness.
㐱 (zhěn) gives the sound — an exact match with 诊.
斤 (an axe) — cutting through something.
米 (grain, in the simplified form; a bundle of thread in the traditional 斷) — the material being cut, giving 断 its meaning 'to break off, cut, sever.'

example.hanzi: 医生根据检查结果做出了准确的诊断。
example.pinyin: yīshēng gēnjù jiǎnchá jiéguǒ zuòchūle zhǔnquè de zhěnduàn.
example.english: The doctor made an accurate diagnosis based on the test results.
example.fact: Stethoscopes were invented in 1816 by French physician René Laennec, who reportedly rolled a sheet of paper into a tube to listen to a patient's heart without pressing his ear directly against her chest, a practice considered improper at the time — his simple wooden tube design remained largely unchanged in principle for over a century.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 撤 describes a physical action of pulling back or removing something, such as troops or an order.
The remaining element on the right historically supplied a now-drifted pronunciation clue; over time the two parts fused into the meaning 'to withdraw, to remove.'
辶 (to walk) — 退 relates to moving backward or away
艮 (gèn) gives a sound distantly related to 退's reading tuì, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 军队在深夜悄悄撤退到山后。
example.pinyin: jūnduì zài shēnyè qiāoqiāo chètuì dào shān hòu.
example.english: The army quietly retreated behind the mountain in the dead of night.
example.fact: The Dunkirk evacuation of 1940 rescued over 330,000 Allied soldiers from the beaches of northern France in just nine days, using a mix of Royal Navy destroyers and hundreds of civilian fishing boats and pleasure craft — an operation originally expected by British commanders to save only about 45,000 troops.

components.note: 女 (woman) — in ancient China, family names traced descent through the mother's line, tying 姓 to the woman radical.
生 (shēng) gives a sound distantly related to xìng, having drifted apart over time.
夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'

example.hanzi: 请在表格上填写你的姓名和出生日期。
example.pinyin: qǐng zài biǎogé shàng tiánxiě nǐ de xìngmíng hé chūshēng rìqī.
example.english: Please fill in your full name and date of birth on the form.
example.fact: Iceland's naming system still largely follows the old Norse patronymic tradition, so most Icelanders have no inherited surname at all — a person's "last name" is typically their father's or mother's first name plus "-son" or "-dóttir," which is why the country's phone directory is alphabetized by first name.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 奶 relates to a woman nursing, and to milk.
乃 (nǎi) is an exact match for the sound of 奶.
氵 (water) — 油 names an oily liquid.
由 (yóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 油.

example.hanzi: 蛋糕上挤满了雪白的奶油。
example.pinyin: dàngāo shàng jǐmǎnle xuěbái de nǎiyóu.
example.english: The cake was piled high with snow-white cream.
example.fact: Butter churning was independently discovered across many ancient pastoral cultures, and Tibetan butter tea, made by churning yak butter, salt, and tea together, has been a staple at high altitude for over a thousand years because the fat provides quick, dense calories in an environment where crops barely grow.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 沿 originally meant following the edge of a river, later extended to 'along' any path or course.
着 developed from 著, whose top originally pictured 羊 (sheep) atop 目 (eye) — a herder keeping an eye fixed on a flock.
目 (eye) — that image of steady, fixed attention gave 着 its meanings 'to attach, to touch, to wear,' and, as a grammatical particle, marking an action still in progress.

example.hanzi: 我们沿着河边散步,欣赏两岸的风景。
example.pinyin: wǒmen yánzhe hébiān sànbù, xīnshǎng liǎng'àn de fēngjǐng.
example.english: We walked along the riverbank, enjoying the scenery on both sides.
example.fact: The Amazon River has no bridges crossing its main channel anywhere along its nearly 6,400-kilometer length, largely because the surrounding rainforest has too few roads to justify one in the first place — most crossings are made by ferry.

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'
父 (father) — 爷 belongs to the family of words for male elders.
耶 (yé) gives the sound — an exact match with 爷's reading yé.

example.hanzi: 老天爷终于下雨了,农民们松了一口气。
example.pinyin: lǎotiānyé zhōngyú xiàyǔle, nóngmínmen sōngle yī kǒu qì.
example.english: Heavens, it finally rained, and the farmers breathed a sigh of relief.
example.fact: Rainmaking rituals appear across nearly every ancient agricultural civilization, from Hopi rain dances in the American Southwest to Chinese dragon-worship ceremonies for rain during drought — a reflection of how directly early societies' survival depended on rainfall timing that they had no scientific way to predict or control.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 悲 relates to a heavy, sorrowful heart.
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to bēi, having drifted apart over time.
忄 (heart) — 惨 describes a heart-wrenching, miserable feeling.
参 (cān) gives a sound very close to cǎn, sharing the initial and rhyme — only the tone differs.

example.hanzi: 战争给这个村庄带来了悲惨的命运。
example.pinyin: zhànzhēng gěi zhège cūnzhuāng dàiláile bēicǎn de mìngyùn.
example.english: The war brought a tragic fate to this village.
example.fact: The 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora in Indonesia was the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded history, ejecting so much ash into the atmosphere that it caused a "Year Without a Summer" in 1816, leading to crop failures, famine, and tens of thousands of deaths across Europe and North America.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — 资 relates to wealth, funds, and resources.
次 (cì) gives a hint of the sound — 资 is pronounced zī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
氵 (water) — 源 originally referred to the spring where a river begins
原 (yuán) gives the sound — an exact match with 源's reading yuán

example.hanzi: 水是地球上最宝贵的自然资源之一。
example.pinyin: shuǐ shì dìqiú shàng zuì bǎoguì de zìrán zīyuán zhī yī.
example.english: Water is one of the most precious natural resources on Earth.
example.fact: Although roughly 71% of Earth's surface is covered in water, only about 0.5% of it is accessible fresh water suitable for drinking, since most is seawater or locked away in glaciers and deep groundwater — a scarcity that has made freshwater access a growing point of geopolitical tension in arid regions.

components.note: 瓦 (tile, earthenware) shows 瓶 is typically made of ceramic or glass.
并 (bìng) gives a sound close to píng, differing mainly in the initial consonant.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他把写好的信放进瓶子,扔进了大海。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ xiěhǎo de xìn fàng jìn píngzi, rēng jìnle dàhǎi.
example.english: He put the finished letter into a bottle and threw it into the sea.
example.fact: The longest-known drifting message in a bottle was found in 2018 on a German beach 132 years after it was tossed into the sea in 1886 as part of a Marine Biological Association experiment studying ocean currents — the postcard inside was still legible enough to identify the ship that released it.

components.note: Opposite/contrary — rebellion means going against something.
Gives the sound bàn, related to pàn but drifted apart over time.
彳 pictures a person's legs walking.
走 (to walk/run) reinforces the idea of movement, giving 徒 its meanings 'on foot' and 'a follower who walks in someone's footsteps.'

example.hanzi: 历史书上把他描述成一个可耻的叛徒。
example.pinyin: lìshǐ shū shàng bǎ tā miáoshù chéng yī gè kěchǐ de pàntú.
example.english: History books describe him as a shameful traitor.
example.fact: Benedict Arnold, once one of George Washington's most trusted generals in the American Revolutionary War, defected to the British side in 1780 after feeling passed over for promotion and facing debt — his name became so synonymous with betrayal in the United States that it is still used today as a common insult for anyone who switches sides.

components.note: 成 traces back to an oracle-bone picture of a halberd-like weapon with an added stroke, likely marking the finishing blow that ended a battle or campaign. That sense of a task being brought to a close gave 成 its meaning 'to complete, to succeed.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 在这个国家,十八岁就被视为成人。
example.pinyin: zài zhège guójiā, shíbā suì jiù bèi shìwéi chéngrén.
example.english: In this country, eighteen is considered the age of adulthood.
example.fact: The legal age of adulthood varies widely across the world — Scotland has historically set the age for many legal contracts at just 16, while Japan lowered its age of adult majority from 20 to 18 only as recently as 2022, showing how much this line is a social choice rather than a fixed biological one.

components.note: 木 (wood) — early models and molds were often carved from wood
莫 (mò) gives a sound close to 模's reading mó, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
弋 (an awl or tool) — one of the craftsman's instruments.
工 (a measuring square) — a tool for making things to a fixed pattern, giving 式 its meaning 'style, form, type.'

example.hanzi: 这家公司正在尝试一种全新的商业模式。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī zhèngzài chángshì yī zhǒng quánxīn de shāngyè móshì.
example.english: This company is trying out a brand-new business model.
example.fact: Netflix's original business model in 1997 was DVD-by-mail rental with no late fees, a pattern that seemed radical against Blockbuster's late-fee-dependent stores — Blockbuster actually turned down a chance to buy Netflix for $50 million in 2000 and filed for bankruptcy just eleven years later.

components.note: 又 (hand, here standing in for 奚, part of the original character) — a simplified stroke that no longer pictures anything on its own.
鸟 (bird) — combined with the simplified left side, 鸡 names a specific 'kind of bird,' the chicken.
冂 traces the outer outline of a cut of meat.
仌 depicts the muscle fibers or ribs inside, together forming a picture of a piece of meat.

example.hanzi: 这道菜用的是新鲜的鸡肉和青椒。
example.pinyin: zhè dào cài yòng de shì xīnxiān de jīròu hé qīngjiāo.
example.english: This dish uses fresh chicken and green peppers.
example.fact: Chickens are the most numerous bird on the planet, with an estimated global population exceeding 25 billion at any given time — outnumbering humans by more than three to one — and archaeologists trace their domestication from wild red junglefowl in Southeast Asia back at least 3,500 years.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick) — 教 relates to instructing or disciplining, the traditional action of teaching.
孝 (xiào) gives a hint of the sound — 教 is pronounced jiào, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'

example.hanzi: 这位教师在乡村小学教了三十年书。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi jiàoshī zài xiāngcūn xiǎoxué jiāole sānshí nián shū.
example.english: This teacher taught at a rural elementary school for thirty years.
example.fact: Finland, often cited as having one of the world's most effective education systems, requires all primary school teachers to hold a master's degree and accepts fewer than 10% of applicants into its teacher training programs, treating the profession with a selectivity comparable to medicine or law in many other countries.

components.note: A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

士 is traditionally read as a picture of a broad-bladed axe or tool, a mark of a capable man entrusted with a task. That association with skill and standing gave 士 its meanings 'scholar, gentleman' and, in military ranks, 'non-commissioned officer.'

example.hanzi: 那位中士带领新兵进行了体能训练。
example.pinyin: nà wèi zhōngshì dàilǐng xīnbīng jìnxíngle tǐnéng xùnliàn.
example.english: That sergeant led the new recruits through physical training.
example.fact: The chevron insignia used to denote sergeant rank in many modern militaries originated in medieval heraldry, where the inverted-V shape symbolized a roof rafter or protection, and was formally adopted by the British Army in 1802 to visually distinguish non-commissioned officers on the battlefield.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 忽 describes a mental state, a sudden shift in attention.
勿 (wù) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading hū has diverged.
田 (field) — 略 originally related to surveying or dividing farmland
各 (gè) gives a sound distantly related to 略's reading lüè, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 我们不能忽略气候变化带来的长期影响。
example.pinyin: wǒmen bùnéng hūlüè qìhòu biànhuà dàilái de chángqī yǐngxiǎng.
example.english: We cannot ignore the long-term effects brought by climate change.
example.fact: The Keeling Curve, a continuous record of atmospheric carbon dioxide measured atop Mauna Loa in Hawaii since 1958, is one of the longest unbroken environmental datasets in existence and was nearly defunded multiple times in its early decades before its long-term significance for tracking climate change was widely recognized.

components.note: The traditional form 風 combined 虫 (insect) with a phonetic element, reflecting an old belief that insects emerged and multiplied on the wind each spring. The simplified 风 preserves only an abstract outline of that older character.
日 here pictures a person's head.
共 pictures two hands; together with the shape below, they depict a violent struggle, giving 暴 its meaning 'violent, sudden.'

example.hanzi: 一场巨大的风暴摧毁了整个渔村。
example.pinyin: yī chǎng jùdà de fēngbào cuīhuǐle zhěnggè yúcūn.
example.english: A huge storm destroyed the entire fishing village.
example.fact: Typhoon Tip, which formed over the Pacific Ocean in October 1979, remains the largest tropical cyclone ever recorded, with a diameter of about 2,220 kilometers — roughly the size of the continental United States east of the Mississippi — though its size did not translate into the highest wind speeds ever measured.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

The ancient graph for 于 is thought to have depicted a curved pipe or wind instrument, its original picture borrowed early on purely for its sound. That borrowed use displaced the original meaning entirely, leaving 于 as a grammatical word meaning 'at, in, to.'

example.hanzi: 这个决定是基于大量的市场调查数据做出的。
example.pinyin: zhège juédìng shì jīyú dàliàng de shìchǎng diàochá shùjù zuòchū de.
example.english: This decision was made based on a large amount of market research data.
example.fact: The Richter scale, developed by Charles Richter in 1935, is based on a logarithmic formula in which each whole-number increase represents roughly 31.6 times more energy release — meaning a magnitude 7 earthquake releases about a thousand times more energy than a magnitude 5, not just two units' worth.

components.note: 西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).

example.hanzi: 淘金热吸引了大批移民前往美国西部。
example.pinyin: táojīnrè xīyǐnle dàpī yímín qiánwǎng měiguó xībù.
example.english: The gold rush attracted large numbers of immigrants to the American West.
example.fact: The California Gold Rush that began in 1848 drew roughly 300,000 people to the American West within a few years, transforming San Francisco from a settlement of about 1,000 residents into a city of 25,000 by 1850 — one of the fastest urban growth rates in recorded history.

components.note: 页 (head) — 预 relates to looking ahead or foreseeing beforehand
予 (yǔ) gives a sound close to 预's reading yù, differing mainly in tone
氵 (water) — 测 originally referred to measuring the depth of water.
则 (zé) gives a rhyme close to cè, with the tone and initial shifted.

example.hanzi: 气象局预测明天将有大雨。
example.pinyin: qìxiàngjú yùcè míngtiān jiāng yǒu dàyǔ.
example.english: The weather bureau predicts heavy rain tomorrow.
example.fact: Modern weather forecasting owes much of its accuracy to Edward Lorenz's 1961 discovery of chaos theory, when he found that rounding a computer's atmospheric simulation input from six decimal places to three produced wildly different long-term weather predictions — the origin of the popular "butterfly effect" metaphor.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
阝 (a mound/formation) — soldiers arranged in position
车 (chariot) — war chariots lined up in formation

example.hanzi: 窗外突然传来一阵急促的敲门声。
example.pinyin: chuāng wài tūrán chuánlái yī zhèn jícù de qiāomén shēng.
example.english: A burst of urgent knocking suddenly came from outside the window.
example.fact: Woodpeckers can peck a tree at over 20 times per second during a single burst, and their skulls have evolved a spongy bone structure and a tongue that wraps around the brain like a seatbelt to absorb the shock — decelerating each strike fast enough that it would otherwise cause a concussion in most other animals.
